text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. 

The patient reports fever and altered mentation but explicitly denies the "severe headache" and "neck stiffness" I asked about in my previous question. This clinical picture, combined with his history of taking haloperidol and reporting rigors without chills, strongly suggests Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome rather than meningitis or encephalitis. I will now request the necessary laboratory results to confirm this diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, CK, and Blood_Culture.
